title: Inventory store with a small JSON API
prompt:
Build an inventory service in Python (standard library only, sqlite3 for storage) as a package inventory/ with inventory/__init__.py, inventory/store.py and inventory/api.py.
- inventory/store.py: class Store(path=":memory:") backed by SQLite. add_item(name, qty, price_cents) -> the new item's id (1, 2, ...); a name that already exists raises ValueError. get(id) -> {"id", "name", "qty", "price_cents"} or None. update_qty(id, delta) -> the updated item; if qty would go below 0 it raises ValueError and changes nothing; an unknown id raises KeyError. list_items(low=None) -> all items ordered by id, or only items with qty < low. delete(id) -> True if it existed, else False.
- inventory/api.py: handle(store, method, path, body=None) -> (status, data), where body and data are plain Python values (dicts/lists) as if parsed from JSON:
  GET /items -> (200, list); GET /items?low=5 -> (200, items with qty < 5); POST /items with {"name", "qty", "price_cents"} -> (201, the item), a missing field -> (400, {"error": ...}), a duplicate name -> (409, {"error": ...}); GET /items/ID -> (200, item) or (404, {"error": "not found"}); PATCH /items/ID with {"delta": n} -> (200, item), (400, {"error": ...}) if it would go below zero, (404, ...) if unknown; DELETE /items/ID -> (204, None) or (404, {"error": "not found"}); anything else -> (404, {"error": "not found"}).
Write unit tests too.
